free_tier.stated: translated from the CNB pricing table, read 2026-10-22: cloud-native build CPU free quota 160 core-hours a month; cloud-native development CPU free quota 1,600 core-hours a month; cloud-native build GPU free quota 0 core-hours a month; cloud-native development GPU free quota 0 core-hours a month; GPU overage at CNY 0.5 per core-hour; repository storage 100 GiB; object storage 100 GiB; 500 AI credits a month.

egress.terms: not published: the billing table on the pricing page lists repository storage, object storage, build and dev CPU and GPU core-hours and AI Credits, and no egress or traffic item

interface_detail: REST (OpenAPI at api.cnb.cool), Git over HTTPS with an access token, and the browser cloud IDE; Git over SSH is documented as unsupported
tooling: a Git client over HTTPS (username cnb, an access token as the password); the REST OpenAPI at api.cnb.cool; the CNB CLI (command cnb, npm package @cnbcool/cnb-cli or Docker image cnbcool/cnb-cli, login by OAuth2 device flow or the CNB_TOKEN variable)
chaining: 1,600 CPU core-hours a month runs a continuous build and test loop for one person, and it holds the build step of any chain whose GPU step has moved elsewhere.

limits.value: 1,600 core-hours a month of development allowance is the only lane left, because the GPU lane went from a quota to zero on 2026-08-01 and a build that needs a card now bills from the first core-hour.

evidence.proved: the pricing table: build CPU 160 core-hours a month free, development CPU 1,600 core-hours a month free, both GPU lines 0 core-hours a month free, storage 100 GiB for repositories and 100 GiB for objects

quoted announcement, translated: from 2026-08-01 CNB cancels the free quota for cloud-native build GPU and cloud-native development GPU; GPU moves to pay-as-you-go; organizations without a bound Tencent Cloud budget cannot use GPU at all until they bind one
the pre-withdrawal state, translated: a .cnb.yaml can request the cnb amd64 GPU L40 tag, giving a shared L40 with more than 40 GB of VRAM, with a single session of at most 4 hours

an account's own quota panel showing a development GPU monthly quota of 1,600 core-hours, then a reply noting the announcement cancels it, then an answer on 2026-08-01 saying the GPU still works, which is a rollout lag and not a revocation
the billing table ends with AI Credits and has no egress or traffic row
